assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes (provisional on emission, confidence 0.75) - daemon_capability: full (confidence 0.85, fix landed + red-first test) - driver_capability: gap:seed_instruction (confidence 0.9) -> route **driver-gap**.

## agent_supports: yes

The scenario is not a muse feature flag; it tests whether muse (1) loads a persistent instruction file the way CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md does for claudecode/codex, and (2) will follow a rule in that file to emit ordinary transcript-visible text (a fenced HTML comment). Both hold for muse:

1. **Muse loads a persistent AGENTS.md project-rules file.** `strings` on the installed CLI binary (`/Users/ingo/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`, Muse Code 1.2.1-R2847.1) contains the literal `muse init`-generated template: `# AGENTS.md\nMuse Code reads this file as project rules when it runs in this directory.` -- confirming AGENTS.md is muse's own native persistent-instruction convention (the binary also documents CLAUDE.md as a *lower-priority* fallback and a one-time `/rules import` source from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`/`$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`, distinct from the native per-project AGENTS.md this recipe targets). The binary also carries the literal runtime injection shape: `<system-reminder source="rules-file"><rules-file scope="" written-for="Muse Code ..."> ... loaded standing rules at session open. Follow higher-priority instructions first. If user and project rules conflict, project rules win. If project rules files conflict, the deeper file wins over the shallower one.</rules-file>` -- so the file is injected as a labelled system-reminder block muse is instructed to obey, structurally the same shape as codex's `<INSTRUCTIONS>` wrapper. This is independently corroborated by the LIVE corpus: muse-format-spec.md section 11 documents a real `context_block_diagnostic{block_id:"rules_file",source:"rules_file",lifecycle:"session_start",action:"observed",text_bytes:1227}` record from an actual captured session -- muse really does load and account for a rules file at session start on this machine, not just in the binary's static strings. And `--trust-workspace` (already passed by `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`, line ~241-242) is required for the rules file to load at all: the binary's own string is explicit -- "exists, but the workspace is untrusted, so it is skipped for this session; restart with --trust-workspace to load project rules" -- so the existing driver clears that precondition for free.
2. **The marker itself is ordinary text.** The daemon parser does not care how the marker text reaches the transcript, only that it lands there; muse is an unrestricted LLM chat/tool-use agent with no observed output filter on assistant prose (parser.go's `parseAssistantMessageCommitted` surfaces the full, unfiltered `event.text`).

What stays PROVISIONAL (hence 0.75, not higher, matching the sibling band): whether muse's configured model (muse-spark-1.3-contributor in the live corpus) reliably RE-EMITS the marker turn-over-turn with climbing completed_rounds is a model-behaviour question the 2026-05-31 experiment (claudecode/sonnet only) does not answer, and only a live recording can settle -- the same caveat every sibling cell (codex/aider/hermes/opencode/pi/copilot) carries. Whether muse's rules-file injection strips or otherwise mangles a bare HTML comment before the model sees it (the concern the scenario's process step 1 exists to guard against) is UNRESOLVED from the binary strings alone -- no evidence of stripping was found, but none of verbatim pass-through either (contrast codex, where the literal `<INSTRUCTIONS>...</INSTRUCTIONS>` wrapper template proves verbatim byte pass-through). The recipe follows the scenario's own mandatory mitigation (wrap the marker example in a fenced code block) regardless, so this does not block agent=yes, but it is named as a caveat / vacuous-pass guard.

## daemon_capability: full (UPDATED — was `bug`)

**The daemon fix landed.** Commit `10e0c6554` ("feat(muse): close four parser gaps -- task estimate, todos, background, retry") wires the missing call directly at the site this cell's prior assessment cited: `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:675` (`parseAssistantMessageCommitted`) now reads

```go
if est := tailer.ScanTaskEstimate(text, ev.Timestamp); est != nil {
    ev.TaskEstimate = est
}
ev.AssistantText = tailer.TruncateAssistantText(text)
```

-- i.e. the FULL, un-truncated `text` is scanned via the shared `tailer.ScanTaskEstimate` BEFORE `TruncateAssistantText` drops everything past 200 runes, satisfying `TruncateAssistantText`'s own documented contract (`core/pkg/tailer/parser.go`: "Adapters MUST scan the full text for markers (ScanTaskEstimate) BEFORE calling this") and matching the exact ordering codex/aider/opencode/pi already use. `ev.TaskEstimate` is now set on the same struct `record`'s verify step reads.

**This is red-first, not a green-that-was-never-red claim.** The commit's own message states the pre-fix symptom verbatim ("Red: `expected TaskEstimate from full-text scan`"), and the added test `TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_TaskEstimate_SurvivesTruncation` (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser_test.go`) feeds a marker followed by 50 filler sentences -- long enough that the marker would fall outside the 200-rune truncation window if the scan ran on the truncated text instead of the full text -- and asserts `TaskEstimate.TotalRounds==6 && CompletedRounds==2`. I re-ran it directly rather than trusting the commit message: `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -run TestParseLine -v` -- `--- PASS: TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_TaskEstimate_SurvivesTruncation (0.00s)`, alongside the rest of the package's `TestParseLine_*` suite, all green.

This closes the gap in exactly the shape `1ae457d9` closed it for codex/pi/aider/opencode -- the same shared, adapter-agnostic `tailer.ScanTaskEstimate` wired into an adapter's existing full-text extraction call site, no new field types or schema changes.

**What this does NOT yet settle:** there is still no LIVE muse recording of this scenario -- the fix is proven against a synthetic unit-test payload, not against a real muse transcript carrying a marker the model actually emitted. That is the driver pillar's job to unblock (below); once `record` ports `seed_instruction` and records this cell, the recording is the first live confirmation that `ev.TaskEstimate` survives an actual muse session end-to-end.

## driver_capability: gap:seed_instruction (verdict UNCHANGED, one citation corrected)

Scenario process step 1 requires the marker rule to be installed as a PERSISTENT INSTRUCTION FILE before the recipe's first prompt (not folded into the first `send`, which some sibling cells did as a workaround but which collapses the very thing this scenario is meant to exercise -- see caveats). Muse's persistent instruction file is a project-root `AGENTS.md`, read "as project rules when it runs in this directory" (confirmed above).

**Citation correction (this pass).** The prior assessment quoted `driver_step_types_from_file`'s output for muse as `exit_clean, interrupt, keys, reset_session, restart, resume, send, session, sigkill, slash, sleep, start_session, wait_turn`. That helper was over-reporting: `interrupt`, `keys`, `reset_session`, and `resume` are `case` arms in `driver-interactive.sh` whose bodies call `not_implemented` (which aborts the run with `nonzero(3)`), not handled step types -- commit `3c3cb8adb` ("fix(onboarding): a not_implemented stub is not a handled driver step type") fixed the helper to exclude stub arms, and its own commit message names this exact cell as the concrete casualty: "muse's own 5-8_task-estimate-marker assessment quotes the over-reported set verbatim." Re-run against the corrected helper (`source tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/lib/recipe-lint.sh; driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`), muse's REAL step-type set is: `exit_clean, restart, send, session, sigkill, slash, sleep, start_session, wait_turn` -- nine types, not thirteen. This does NOT change the verdict here: `seed_instruction` was absent from both the (wrong) reported set and the corrected one, so the gap this cell has always carried was never in question -- only the surrounding evidence was overstated and is now fixed.

**`seed_instruction` is implemented by no driver in the repo.** `grep -l seed_instruction replaydata/agents/*/driver-*.sh tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/templates/*.tmpl` returns zero matches -- not muse's driver, not any sibling driver, and not the shared scaffold template (`tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/templates/drive-interactive.sh.tmpl`), whose own "standard step types" comment block (lines 34-47) enumerates `send/slash/wait_turn/interrupt/keys/sleep/reset_session/restart/resume/sigkill/exit_clean/start_session/session` and nothing resembling `seed_instruction`. This is not a "port from a reference driver" gap like the other stub arms above (which at least have a working claudecode/codex/gemini-cli exemplar to copy) -- the primitive has to be designed from first principles.

**Five adapters' `5-8_task-estimate-marker` cells wait on this exact primitive**, confirmed by reading each cell's `driver_capability` field directly: `codex`, `copilot`, `muse`, `opencode`, `pi` all carry `driver_capability: gap:seed_instruction` today (the remaining cells with a recipe for this scenario -- aider/antigravity/claudecode/gemini-cli/hermes -- show `driver=ready` only because their recipes use the fold-into-first-`send` workaround instead, not because they implement this step). Designing `seed_instruction` once therefore unblocks five matrix columns at once, not just this cell.

**Recommendation: the step belongs in the SHARED template, not per-driver.** Every other stubbed arm in `drive-interactive.sh.tmpl` (`wait_turn`, `interrupt`, `keys`, `reset_session`, `restart`, `resume`, `sigkill`, `exit_clean`, `start_session`, `session`) is marked `TODO(__AGENT__)` because its mechanics are genuinely agent-specific -- a tmux keystroke sequence, a transcript-polling loop, a CLI restart invocation. `seed_instruction` is categorically different: writing the recipe step's own `text` field to `$RUN_CWD/<path>` before `start_session` is pure filesystem I/O (`printf '%s' "$text" > "$RUN_CWD/$path"`), identical for every agent, requiring zero access to tmux or the agent's own CLI surface -- the same shape as the template's already-present, zero-porting `send`/`slash`/`sleep` arms rather than its `not_implemented`-stubbed ones. Confirming this empirically: I read all five waiting cells' `seed_instruction` steps directly (codex/copilot/opencode/pi/muse), and every one of them already targets the SAME filename in its `path` field -- `"AGENTS.md"` -- so there is not even a per-driver filename to parameterize beyond what the recipe already carries. One dispatch-loop arm added to the shared template once (mirroring `RUN_CWD`'s existing per-run staging), inherited automatically by every driver scaffolded from it going forward and back-ported once to each of the five already-generated `driver-interactive.sh` files, unblocks all five columns -- versus five separate from-scratch implementations if left per-driver. Muse's own instruction file is `AGENTS.md`, per the `muse init` template string already cited under agent_supports.

## Route

agent=yes + (daemon=full, driver=gap:*) -> **driver-gap** per the routing table (driver gap takes precedence over the daemon full/bug distinction, so the route itself does not change even though the daemon pillar just moved from `bug` to `full`). The recipe + spec are both re-authored now so `record` can proceed the moment it ports `seed_instruction` -- the daemon side needs no further work for this cell; only the driver-side primitive remains.
caveats: agent=yes is PROVISIONAL on emission: no live recording has ever driven muse to emit or advance this marker. The 2026-05-31 marker experiment that established 0% exact-format compliance (motivating the parser's tolerant key-drift acceptance) was claudecode/sonnet only.

Whether muse's <rules-file> injection passes a bare HTML comment through verbatim (vs. stripping/rendering it, the way some agents' Markdown pipelines strip bare HTML comments) is UNRESOLVED from binary strings alone -- no stripping behavior was found, but none confirming verbatim byte pass-through either (contrast codex's literal <INSTRUCTIONS>...</INSTRUCTIONS> template, which settled the question directly for that adapter). The recipe follows the scenario's own mandated mitigation (fence the marker example in a code block) regardless, so this is a defensive default, not a resolved fact.

Vacuous-pass guard: the phase DSL alone (ready->working->ready) would still pass if muse never emitted a valid marker at all -- an ordinary multi-turn session produces the same state arc with or without the marker mechanism working. The real assertions (task_estimate values, non-decreasing completed_rounds, burning-down eta, suppressed-at-ready) are NOT expressible in the phase DSL and must be checked by hand against the recording's session-metrics API by whoever runs `record`, per the recipe's verify[] list -- exactly as codex/hermes/aider/opencode do for their own sibling cells.

daemon=full is now proven by a red-first unit test (TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_TaskEstimate_SurvivesTruncation, re-run and confirmed PASS this pass) against a synthetic payload, NOT yet by a live muse recording of this scenario -- there is still no recording of this cell (driver-gap blocks it). The daemon-side risk this cell originally flagged is closed; what remains open is the driver-side gap below.

cost_nonzero is pinned false per the muse-wide, corpus-verified fact that no dollar cost is ever persisted in a muse transcript (muse-format-spec.md's recursive JSON-key scan) -- this is a muse-wide constant, not specific to this cell, and must not be read as a defect of the marker mechanism.

model is pinned to muse-spark-1.3-contributor from live corpus evidence used consistently across the other already-assessed muse cells (e.g. token-accounting), not from vendor docs -- re-verify at record time in case a different model is the session default when this actually records.

seed_instruction is implemented by no driver in the repo and is not present in the shared scaffold template either (grep -l seed_instruction replaydata/agents/*/driver-*.sh tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/templates/*.tmpl -> zero matches) -- it must be designed, not ported from an existing exemplar. Five cells wait on it (codex, copilot, muse, opencode, pi); recommend implementing it ONCE in tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/templates/drive-interactive.sh.tmpl as a zero-porting dispatch-loop arm (pure filesystem I/O, agent-independent) rather than five separate per-driver ports -- see the driver_capability section for the full argument. Muse's own target file is AGENTS.md, matching the other four waiting cells' recipes, which already target the same filename.

Sibling precedent for both the daemon-fix shape and the driver=gap:seed_instruction verdict; this assessment's structure and recipe are adapted from it. Codex's own cell is already daemon=full / driver=gap:seed_instruction / confidence 0.8, the pattern this re-assessment aligns muse's cell to.
Committed precedent for muse's single-birth phase model (no ProcessMatcher/presession split), reused for this cell's phase DSL.

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login or META_API_KEY) -- confirmed installed at 1.2.1 on this machine
irrlichd is recording (--attach or isolated coexist mode)
the default muse model/preset is muse-spark-1.3-contributor or another model that reliably follows a project-rules instruction -- re-probe at record time if a different preset is pinned

Driver already mints a fresh per-run cwd under $STAGING/cwd and launches with --trust-workspace (driver-interactive.sh), so the seeded AGENTS.md loads without the untrusted-workspace modal blocking it

RECIPE CORRECTION (record, pre-live-run, 2026-09-15): dropped a stray {"type":"start_session"} step that followed seed_instruction in the originally-assessed script. Cross-checked against all four sibling recipes for this scenario (codex/copilot/opencode/pi) -- none of them has an explicit session-launch step between seed_instruction and the first send; codex/copilot/pi go straight to send, opencode uses its own headless-to-live "live" step. The assessment setup note ("write ... to $RUN_CWD/AGENTS.md BEFORE start_session, mirroring the codex/copilot/opencode/pi sibling recipes") used "start_session" as prose for "the agent launching", not the literal start_session STEP TYPE -- driver-interactive.sh already launches slot 1 unconditionally via launch_repl before the step loop runs, so a literal start_session step here would allocate a SPURIOUS second concurrent session and switch $ACTIVE onto it (step_start_session, no explicit cwd, defaults new_cwd to $RUN_CWD -- so it would not even fail loudly, just add an untracked idle session and move all subsequent sends onto a second session_id, breaking the scenario single-session arc the spec asserts). Removed for parity with the sibling recipes; the new pre-launch seed_instruction pass in driver-interactive.sh (#1960) writes AGENTS.md into $RUN_CWD before launch_repl fires, which is the only launch this scenario needs.

script.text:
# AGENTS.md

## Task progress marker (irrlicht)

While working a multi-phase task, emit a hidden progress marker in your own reply text on EVERY turn, exactly in this form (keep it as an HTML comment so it stays out of the rendered answer):

```
<!-- {"marker":"irrlicht-eta","total_rounds":N,"completed_rounds":M} -->
```

Set total_rounds to the number of phases you plan. Emit it with completed_rounds=0 on your first reply, then increase completed_rounds by 1 each turn as you finish a phase, until completed_rounds == total_rounds on the final turn.

Plan a 4-phase refactor of a small Python module: (1) read and summarize the file, (2) propose the change, (3) apply it, (4) verify. Treat each phase as one round. As instructed in AGENTS.md, emit the irrlicht-eta progress marker in your reply on every turn, starting now with completed_rounds=0 and total_rounds=4. Begin phase 1 and stop; I will say 'next' to advance.
next -- this is the final phase; report the task done and emit the marker with completed_rounds=4.

verify: While the session is working, session metrics carry task_estimate {total_rounds:4, completed_rounds:M} matching the values muse reported in its marker (completed_rounds <= total_rounds).
task_estimate.updated_at advances each time a fresher marker is observed.
task_estimate.completed_rounds is non-decreasing across turns and reaches 4 on the final working turn.
task_completion_eta is present once completed_rounds >= 1 and a later projection is <= an earlier one (burns down).
task_estimate / task_completion_eta are present only while working; absent at ready.
State topology ready -> working -> ready; final state ready.

The daemon fix landed (10e0c6554): muse's parseAssistantMessageCommitted now calls tailer.ScanTaskEstimate on the full assistant text before truncation (core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:675-687), matching the codex/aider/opencode/pi wiring, and TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_TaskEstimate_SurvivesTruncation confirms it survives truncation. task_estimate/task_completion_eta should now surface once the seed_instruction driver gap is closed and this cell actually records -- confirm on the first real recording rather than assuming.
